When she won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for the movie Y in 2015, she gave one of the most talked-about speeches in recent history. Instead of just thanking agents, she used her platform to demand equal pay for women and wage equality. 13. In 1858, the University of Calcutta held its first-ever Bachelor of Arts examination with only thirteen candidates appearing for the grueling test. When the results were compiled, the Senate was horrified to find that not a single student had passed every subject. X and his peer had performed brilliantly in most areas but fell short by a few marks in their optional Persian paper. Fearing that failing the entire inaugural class would permanently damage the prestige and credibility of the newly established University, the Senate held an emergency meeting and made the historic decision to award the duo "grace marks." Consequently, X and his peer were declared the first two graduates of the University, proving that even the "Emperor of Literature" benefited from a little bit of administrative leniency at the start of his journey.
